title: Antonios E. Marsellos, Ph.D.

Research with students
I keep part of my research close to the students’ level of study and bring students into team projects, from first exposure to coding all the way to peer-reviewed publication. Student names appear as co-authors across conference proceedings, posters, and journal articles.



  High School Research
  Through the Hofstra University Summer Science Research Program (HUSSRP),
  high school students run real research projects in R (from EEG seizure
  detection to sunspot cycles and GPS ground motion) and present at
  conferences. 18 students in 2024, 27 in 2025, 7 in 2026, and a 2026 IEEE
  conference paper among the outcomes.
  Meet the projects →




  University Research
  Undergraduate and graduate students join independent research studies
  (GEOL-151), honors options, and theses (earlier cohorts joined the
  NSF-funded GEOTeams program, 2021–2023), co-authoring over a hundred
  conference papers and journal articles on floods, earthquakes, volcanoes,
  climate, and AI. New for Fall 2026: a 2-credit Intro to R for Geoscience
  and Sustainability course, with seats still open.

title: Research with University Students
text:
With students at a Hofstra University research poster day.
Undergraduate and graduate students are co-authors, not assistants, in my research group. Since 2015, students at Hofstra University (and previously the University of Brighton and University of Florida) have co-authored more than a hundred conference papers, posters, and peer-reviewed journal articles on floods, earthquakes, volcanoes, climate, groundwater, and AI.

title: Research with University Students
text:
How students join the group

Independent Research Study (GEOL-151): every semester, students run 1–3 credit individual projects. Recent topics include a live R–GIS earthquake monitoring system for New York, sandstorm detection with GIS, hurricane periodicity forecasting, sunspot–temperature analysis, LiDAR erosion mapping of Long Island, and AI for K-12 Earth science education.
New for Fall 2026: Intro to R for Geoscience and Sustainability (Earth Data Analytics): a 2-credit course that starts from zero coding experience and works with real climate, groundwater, air quality, and map data. No exams: weekly hands-on work and a short final mini-project. Seats are still open for Fall 2026. In this first year it registers as an independent study listing: undergraduates enroll in Independent Special Projects 152-01, graduate students in Graduate Independent Study in Sustainability 251-02.
Honors options (INHO) and theses: individually negotiated honors research, B.S./M.S. theses, and Ph.D. co-supervision.
NSF GEOTeams (2021–2023): the NSF-funded GEOTeams: Summer Research Pathways to Geoscience program (co-PI, award #1911514) built multilevel research teams pairing Hofstra undergraduates with a high school researcher each year, and took students on funded fieldwork to the active volcanoes of Greece: Nisyros, Santorini, and Korinthos.
Conference pipeline: the group presents every year at the Conference on the Geology of Long Island and Metropolitan New York, Hofstra’s Undergraduate and Graduate Research Days, the Mohawk Watershed Symposium, GSA and AGU meetings, and the NJBDA Big Data Symposium.

title: Research with University Students
text:
How to get started
Write to me at antonios.marsellos@hofstra.edu before registration, with a topic idea or with none at all (we can shape one together), then enroll in GEOL-151 or the matching independent study listing in your major. Students majoring in Sustainability are welcome in every research area.

title: Research Areas
text:
My research develops data analytics, artificial intelligence, and computational methods for extracting knowledge from complex spatial and temporal data. The methods come first; sustainability and the environment, earthquakes, volcanoes, floods, climate, biomedical signals, and markets are the applications. Publications often belong to several areas, and every count below links to the filtered publication list.
I teach and advise in the Department of Geology, Environment, and Sustainability at Hofstra University, and students majoring in Sustainability are welcome in every one of these areas. The first area below gathers the environmental and sustainability work: water quality, air quality, flooding, coastal change, emissions, and the data skills that turn those records into evidence. The same skills are taught step by step in my 2026 book R for Earth and Sustainability Data Analytics, written with Dr. Katerina Tsakiri.
I always keep open space for new topics. If you are working on a sustainability question that is not listed here, or you want to bring your own, write to me and we can shape a project around it.

title: About
text:
Biography
I am an Associate Professor in Geo-analytics in the Department of Geology, Environment & Sustainability at Hofstra University (New York) and an Adjunct Associate Professor of Business at Rider University’s Norm Brodsky College of Business, where I teach in the Business Honors Program.
My research develops data analytics, artificial intelligence, and computational methods that draw knowledge out of complex spatial and temporal data. The methods come first, and the applications follow: floods and groundwater, earthquakes and ground movement, volcanic activity, climate and solar signals, biomedical signals, and business analytics.
In 2017 I designed and built the department’s advanced GIS laboratory and its Computer Big Data Laboratory, and both have been in continuous use since. The work there separates long-term, seasonal, and short-term components in very noisy records, using decomposition of time series, Kolmogorov-Zurbenko filtering, and wavelet and spectral analysis, and it forecasts and classifies with artificial neural networks and random forests. The records come from continuous monitoring stations, from geodetic (GNSS, GPS) sensors, and from remote sensing: LiDAR, drone thermal and optical scanning, and InSAR.
Sustainability and the environment run through most of this work: water quality in Hempstead Bay and in New York City harbors, nitrate and contamination signals in Long Island groundwater, flood risk and shoreline change on Fire Island and in the Rockaways, urban flood reconstruction in New York City, particulate contaminants in snowfall and airborne particulate matter during extreme dust events, sinkholes and landslides, and sustainable tourism and farming beside active volcanoes. With students I keep a volcanic monitoring network running on the Hellenic Volcanic Arc at Santorini, Nisyros, and Sousaki, where surface temperature sensors and drone thermal scanning are combined with methods that separate the atmospheric effect from the volcanic signal.
I like to keep part of my research projects close to students’ level of study, bringing students into team projects with enthusiasm and encouraging them to develop their own ideas. High school researchers, undergraduate and graduate students, and the NSF-funded GEOTeams program work with me on real data and present the results at conferences. The same data skills are set out step by step in my book R for Earth and Sustainability Data Analytics, written with Dr. Katerina Tsakiri.

title: About
text:
Research funding

My research and student programs have been supported by more than 30 funded grants, fellowships, and awards since 2006, as principal investigator, co-principal investigator, or collaborator, from funders in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Greece. Highlights:

National Science Foundation (NSF): GEOTeams (IUSE GEOPATHS program), multilevel summer research teams carrying students from high school to graduate level through funded geoscience fieldwork, co-PI (2021–2023, NSF award #1911514)
Long Island Regional Planning Council: two multi-year water quality monitoring and analysis programs for Long Island’s bays, co-PI (2019, 2021)
The New York Community Trust (Long Island Community Foundation): identifying contamination sources in Oyster Bay and Cold Spring Harbor, co-PI (2019)
Hellenic Government (Municipality of Nisyros): upgrading the monitoring of hydrothermal gases and heat distribution on the Nisyros volcano, co-PI (2018)
United Kingdom research schemes (University of Brighton): three continuous GPS stations on the Hellenic arc (Kythera, Peloponnese, Santorini), rare earth element deposit research, and paleo-shoreline mapping for earthquake and tsunami risk assessment, PI and early-career awardee (2013–2015)
Rider University Davis Fellowships: flood forecasting and volcanic surface temperature prediction models, co-PI (2017–2019), and the Applied Business Research Program, a research-to-publication curriculum for the Norm Brodsky College of Business, collaborator (2026–2027)
Hofstra University: Faculty Research Development Grants, Presidential Research Awards, HUSSRP summer research program support, and community-engaged learning grants (PI)
Earlier support from UNESCO, the Geological Society of America, and the Institute of Kytheraismos (Greece)

I have also contributed to funded projects led by colleagues, including an NSF Major Research Instrumentation spectroscopy laboratory at Union College and an American Chemical Society study of radiation damage in zircon.

title: Research with High School Students
text:
With a high school researcher at the students' conference, in front
  of EEG seizure-detection and sunspot-analysis posters.
High school students in my group do real research, not simulations of it. Through the Hofstra University Summer Science Research Program (HUSSRP), students learn R programming from scratch, work with real scientific data, and carry a project from question to conference poster in a single summer, presenting at a Hofstra University conference poster session.

title: Research with High School Students
text:
How the program works
Students meet online through the summer, learning data analysis in R while developing an individual research topic with real datasets: EEG recordings from pediatric seizure patients, continuous GPS displacement, sunspot records, sea-level and groundwater time series, and more. The program culminates in a printed research poster presented at Hofstra University.
The methodology students learn mirrors the group’s research toolkit (time-series decomposition, wavelet analysis, artificial neural networks) and the beginner-first approach of my book R for Earth and Sustainability Data Analytics.

  
    
      
        
    
    
      The book behind the program
      R for Earth and Sustainability Data Analytics follows the same
      beginner-first path the students take: no prior coding or statistics
      experience assumed, working with real Earth and environmental data in R.
      It is recommended reading for students in the program, never required,
      and the opening chapter and the quick-start cheat sheet are free.

title: Research with High School Students
text:
A separate program: NSF GEOTeams (2021–2023)
HUSSRP is not the only route high school students have taken into this group. GEOTeams was a separate program, with separate funding, supported by the NSF (award #1911514). It built multilevel research teams: a faculty mentor, Hofstra undergraduates, and one high school researcher working together on the same scientific question rather than on separate exercises.
One high school researcher joined the team in each of the three years, 2021, 2022 and 2023. Each carried the work through to a conference presentation and appears as a co-author on it. One travelled with the group on the NSF-funded fieldwork to the active volcanoes of Greece.
HUSSRP, which I created and direct, has continued this work since 2024 as a distinct program under separate funding.
